headline: Chips and Software Hit Hard as Oil Shock Rattles Monday's Session
body_html:
Equities are under broad pressure at midday Monday, with decliners outpacing advancers by a margin of roughly 2.6-to-1 across our 544-name universe. The dominant force reshaping the tape is a spike in crude oil prices after President Trump rejected an Iranian peace overture, sending energy-sensitive sectors reeling and draining risk appetite across growth-oriented segments of the market. Healthcare is the lone sector holding its head above water, posting a modest 0.14% gain, while every other sector tracked is in the red.

Semiconductors are bearing the brunt of the selling, off 3.0% as a group mid-session. MongoDB is the standout wreck of the day, plunging 18.52% in the software-database space, while Arm Holdings and Credo Technology have shed 8.82% and 8.77%, respectively, dragging the broader chip complex lower. Bloom Energy has tumbled 9.03%, an outlier within the energy sector, which itself is only marginally negative — suggesting idiosyncratic pressure rather than a pure commodity story for that name.

Against the carnage, consumer-apparel names are posting a surprising pocket of strength. Victoria's Secret leads all gainers at up 5.26%, with Gap Inc. and American Eagle Outfitters adding 3.28% and 3.05%. Into the close, traders will be watching oil's trajectory and any fresh signals on the U.S.-Iran diplomatic track, where officials indicate separate mediated talks could materialize as early as today or Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Trump's Iran Rejection Sends Oil Surging, Wall Street Lower
briefs.body: President Trump's dismissal of an Iranian peace proposal has triggered a sharp rally in crude oil, injecting fresh geopolitical risk into Monday's session. Equities have responded with broad selling pressure, particularly in growth and technology segments. Diplomatic officials say the U.S. and Iran may still hold separate, mediator-facilitated discussions as early as today or Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Semiconductors in Freefall, Sector Off 3% at Midday
briefs.body: The semiconductor sector is the session's hardest-hit group, down 3.0% as a whole. Arm Holdings has surrendered 8.82% and Credo Technology 8.77%, compounding losses across chip-related names. The selloff appears tied to broader risk-off sentiment rather than any single earnings catalyst.

briefs.headline: MongoDB Craters Nearly 19%, Leading Software Decliners
briefs.body: MongoDB shares are the worst performer in the universe mid-session, collapsing 18.52% in heavy volume. The software-database company's steep drop is dragging the broader software sector, itself down 1.12% on the day. No other software name comes close to matching the magnitude of MongoDB's intraday loss.

briefs.headline: Apparel Names Defy the Tape With Sharp Gains
briefs.body: Victoria's Secret, Gap Inc., and American Eagle Outfitters are each climbing more than 3% Monday, forming an unlikely island of strength inside a broadly negative consumer sector. Burlington Stores is also higher by 3.18%, suggesting off-price retail is catching a bid alongside apparel. The moves stand in contrast to the consumer sector's overall 0.71% decline.

briefs.headline: Qatar Flags LNG Supply Disruptions to European and Asian Buyers
briefs.body: Qatar has issued force majeure notices on liquefied natural gas deliveries to Italy's Edison and a number of Asian clients, raising fresh supply concerns in global energy markets. Separately, reports indicate LNG vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has picked up despite ongoing regional tensions. The developments add another layer of complexity to already elevated energy prices.

briefs.headline: UK Airbase Incident: Five British Nationals Bailed After Explosives Probe
briefs.body: Five individuals arrested in connection with an explosives-related investigation near a U.S. airbase in Britain have been released on bail, authorities confirmed Monday. All five have been identified as British nationals. Iran has denied any link to the incident, and the case is drawing close scrutiny from security officials on both sides of the Atlantic.
